thread:
jacob_cust: Hey folks — after we flipped to the VPC endpoint (vpce-0a1b2c3d) for api.redwood.com our production service started throwing intermittent 502s and TLS handshake failures. Seen both 'SSL_connect: error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:sslv3 alert handshake failure' and backend 502s. Worked before endpoint. Can someone help troubleshoot?

anna_support: Sorry you're hitting this — can you paste a minimal repro (curl -v) and a DNS check (dig) from one of your app hosts? Also which region/VPC is this?

jacob_cust: Sure — we are in us-east-1, VPC 10.0.0.0/16. App host is in private subnet with NAT for internet egress. Quick outputs:
```
# dig
$ dig +short api.redwood.com
10.0.5.12

# curl
$ curl -v https://api.redwood.com/health
* Connected to 10.0.5.12 (10.0.5.12) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.2 connection using TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256
* server certificate: CN = gateway.internal.redwood
* TLS alert received: handshake failure
* SSL_connect error
* Closing connection 0
curl: (35) SSL_connect: SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL in connection to api.redwood.com:443 
```
Seems weird — cert shows CN gateway.internal.redwood but the Host header is api.redwood.com. When I run the same curl from my laptop (public internet) it works fine hitting the public ALB IP.

luis_engineer: Two quick possibilities: 1) split-horizon/private hosted zone mismatch (you're resolving to a different endpoint that expects different SNI/host header), or 2) egress allowlist / firewall is blocking OCSP/CRL/OCSP stapling checks or an upstream proxy is altering SNI. Can you run an openssl s_client to see the server cert chain and SNI behavior?

jacob_cust: Ran this from the app host (attached):
```
$ openssl s_client -connect 10.0.5.12:443 -servername api.redwood.com -showcerts
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=0 CN = gateway.internal.redwood
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
---
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=gateway.internal.redwood
   i:/CN=redwood-internal-root
---
SSL handshake has read 2847 bytes and written 397 bytes
---
```
So server presents internal cert (CN gateway.internal.redwood), which doesn't match api.redwood.com. But when I --resolve to public IP it presents a cert with CN=api.redwood.com.

raj_infra: That points to split-horizon PHZ or mis-association: your VPC-private DNS is returning the interface endpoint ENI IP (10.0.5.12) which is the privatelink fronting internal gateway, but that gateway expects client SNI/host header to be the internal name OR it's expecting requests from pinned customers with a specific endpoint policy. Two things to check: 1) is your Route53 private hosted zone for api.redwood.com associated to your VPC? 2) does the endpoint have an endpoint policy restricting principals or methods?

anna_support: Also confirm SGs and NACLs on the vpce ENIs allow the app host ephemeral ports back to the ENI. Sometimes hairpin/NAT setups cause source IP translation and the endpoint rejects the connection because it doesn't see allowed CIDR. If you have a proxy in the path, confirm it passes SNI (socat/proxy can strip it).

jacob_cust: Quick answers: PHZ is associated, that mapping to 10.0.5.12 is expected. We do have an egress allowlist/proxy that routes all outbound traffic through a corporate proxy. Could that be changing SNI? From the app host if I `curl --resolve api.redwood.com:443:10.0.5.12 https://api.redwood.com/health -H 'Host: api.redwood.com'` I get 200. From the app (which uses JVM HttpClient via the corporate proxy) it fails.

luis_engineer: Bingo — corporate proxy/path likely intercepts and either terminates TLS (MITM) or strips SNI when talking to the internal gateway IP. PrivateLink endpoints expect TLS passthrough with correct SNI that maps to the customer-facing certificate. If proxy terminates TLS then the downstream connection to the endpoint gets the wrong SNI or an internal cert. Two repros: 1) test from an EC2 in same subnet but bypass proxy (no proxy env vars) -> does it succeed? 2) run `openssl s_client -connect 10.0.5.12:443 -servername api.redwood.com` from the box that fails path and compare to the box that passes.

jacob_cust: Ran openssl from the app container (which uses proxy): it shows CN=gateway.internal.redwood (same failure). From a test EC2 that bypasses proxy it's CN=api.redwood.com and OK. So proxy is involved.

raj_infra: For a quick workaround, add an egress rule that allows the app hosts to connect directly to the vpce ENI IPs (bypass corporate proxy) or configure the proxy to preserve SNI and not terminate for that destination. Long-term: either use the endpoint's public-facing hostname via the public path or ensure your proxy supports TLS passthrough.

anna_support: Also double-check the endpoint policy — if the endpoint is doing customer-level routing it might expect the original Host header. If proxy rewrites Host, that will break routing and cause 502.

deploy-bot: Deployed gateway v2024.10.22-5 to us-east-1 at 3723413300 — no infra changes for endpoint policies in that release.

jacob_cust: Thanks everyone — bypassing proxy for the endpoint IPs fixed it in staging. We'll work with the network team to enable passthrough for api.redwood.com or allow direct routes to the vpce ENIs. Appreciate the help :thumbsup:

luis_engineer: Good find. If you want, we can also issue a customer-facing CN on the PrivateLink gateway that matches api.redwood.com for future compatibility, but that requires cert provisioning and will need a rollout. For now, proxy passthrough or VPC-specific route is the right path.

anna_support: Marking this thread as resolved unless you need a ticket opened with infra/networking — @raj_infra can help coordinate with the customer's network team if needed. :white_check_mark:
